free_tier.stated: European dedicated bare-metal GPU servers sold by the month, which is the cheapest per-hour shape for a workload that runs continuously. Quoted per-card monthly prices and their 730-hour hourly equivalent at USD 1 = EUR 0.89246: RTX 3090 24GB from EUR 125 per card per month, USD 140.06, USD 0.192/hr; RTX A6000 48GB from EUR 181, USD 202.81, USD 0.278/hr; RTX 4090 24GB from EUR 329, USD 368.64, USD 0.505/hr; RTX 5090 32GB from EUR 336, USD 376.49, USD 0.516/hr; A100 40GB 8x at EUR 363 per card, USD 0.557/hr; L40S 8x at EUR 411, USD 0.631/hr; A100 SXM 80GB 8x at EUR 624, USD 0.958/hr; H100 SXM 8x NVLink at EUR 1,488 per card, USD 1,667.30, USD 2.284/hr; H200 1x at EUR 2,987, USD 4.585/hr. Each server ships with the CPU, RAM, NVMe and 1 Gbit network named on the row; the page states no setup fees.

egress.terms: Storage and network are included in the monthly price on this page; egress terms were not published there and were not established.

limits.value: The one-month commitment on a bare-metal invoice is the binding term, so the USD 0.192 per hour only exists for a workload that occupies the card for most of 730 hours.

notes: New provider: no record in dossier/compute/. Every hourly figure is my division of a published monthly price by 730 hours, and it is a break-even only at full occupancy: at 100 hours a month the same A6000 costs USD 2.03 per hour. A second tracker read the same day prices an RTX A6000 on LeaderGPU at USD 0.44 per hour as a secure on-demand rate, which is 58 percent above my monthly-equivalent and is evidence that the monthly price is a discount against an hourly list rather than the only way this host sells. The 8x rows quote a per-card price with a total beside it, and the total is what an invoice carries, so the smallest orderable unit on those rows is eight cards and not one. Storage and network are included in the monthly price on this page; egress terms were not published there and were not established.
